This Writ Petition Coming On For Preliminary Hearing, This Day, The Court Made The Following: 3 Order
texts.facts: The petitioners are aggrieved by the second respondent's order dated 24.01.2020 seizing the R.O. water plant set up by the first petitioner under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, Aradhya Foundatino Charitable Trusts vs State Of Karnataka on 23 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165497867/ 2 2006 (for short, 'the Act'). 2. It is undisputed that the second respondent has initiated the aforesaid proceeding for seizure of R.O. water units without any notice to the petitioners. The first petitioner, for installation of such water filter plant, has obtained permission from the concerned Gram Panchayath and additionally, the respondent No.3, after testing the water for potability, has issued a Certificate along with endorsement that the water is potable. But, the second respondent, without even as much as a show-cause notice, has seized the water filter units on 24.01.2020. The second respondent should have considered these circumstances.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the first petitioner is a charitable trust and has installed a Water Filter Plant to facilitate pure drinking water to the villagers of Halekote village at low cost as the villagers could be vulnerable to various water borne diseases and other health impediments. 3. The learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that the first petitioner has installed the R.O. water plant for the use of the community on non- profitable basis and does not deal with packaged water. A Certification from Bureau of Indian Standards would be required only when water is sold as packaged drinking water, and if a facility is set up for the benefit of the community for disbursing water in cans, ISI certification would not be required. 4. A Division Bench of this Court in Lochamesh B Hugar v. Union of India and others reported in (2013) 2 KLJ 643, relying upon the provisions of Food and Safety Standards (Food Products, Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, more specifically regulation 2.10.8, has directed the Authorities to ensure that all necessary steps are taken to prohibit, prevent, manufacture and sale of packaged drinking water without Certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards with further directions. The amendment reads as follows: "2.10.8 Packaged Drinking Water (other than mineral water) - 1. means water, other than natural water that is likely to be used for human consumption and that is offered or sold in packaged form, by whatever name it may be called, offered or sold" This Court, in the light of the amended provisions, in a similar matter in W.P.No.45574/2018 has held as under:- "9.
